subject.title: Improve context overflow error message with specifics

question: Which session identity and token-accounting fields may OpenClaw safely expose in channel-visible context-overflow diagnostics?
rationale: The useful implementation boundary is clear, but repository code cannot decide whether raw session/channel identifiers are acceptable or how provider-observed, recorded, and estimated token values should be represented without misleading users.

options.title: Redacted diagnostics
options.body: Show a privacy-safe display label, model and effective budget, and counts explicitly marked as observed or estimated while keeping raw session keys and paths out of user-visible text.

options.title: Budget details only
options.body: Show model, effective budget, count provenance, and recovery actions but omit all session identity from the visible message.

options.title: Keep generic output
options.body: Retain the current generic user message and restrict detailed diagnostics to logs and status tooling.

recommendation.title: Redacted diagnostics
recommendation.body: Show a privacy-safe display label, model and effective budget, and counts explicitly marked as observed or estimated while keeping raw session keys and paths out of user-visible text.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest recent history spans the runner, compaction, and auto-reply decision surfaces that must share this product policy.
